evidence: The hunk matches `case "start", "done", "close", "reopen":` literally while the model exports Action* constants, so a rename would silently zero the counter; the agent switched to the constants.
guidance_note: When a test matches on domain values, reference the exported constants rather than string literals so a rename breaks compilation instead of silently weakening the assertion.

evidence: The comment claims 'wholly untouched — no partial field write, no recorded event' but the code only checks Title and transitionActionCount(added)==0; a field-change event or a description write would pass. The agent asserted every field and a zero total event count.
guidance_note: When a test comment states an invariant ('wholly untouched'), write one assertion per clause of that claim before committing, or narrow the comment to what is asserted.

narrative: This test-only PR got two valid round-0 findings: literal action strings and a rejection-path comment that claimed more than the test asserted. Both fixes were correct and complete, and round 1 was clean.
guidance_observations: Both findings are test-authoring hygiene that a self-review against 'does each comment's claim have an assertion' would have caught before review.

evidence: The doc said openBlockers 'must already be ordered most-direct-first', but openBlockerIDs only does a lexicographic id sort; the 71dd69a diff rewords it to 'a deterministic order'.
guidance_note: When documenting an ordering contract, describe the comparator the code actually uses (id sort for determinism) rather than an intended semantic it does not implement.

evidence: This is the same 'most-direct' misdescription in the openBlockerIDs comment. 71dd69a rewrote it to 'sorted by id so the blocker named in a blocked marker is deterministic', which matches sort.Strings.
guidance_note: When one comment states a wrong contract, grep for the same phrase in its producer and consumer docs before pushing.

evidence: The N+1 is real: there is one GetIssueDetail per child. The agent deferred it to a filed ticket (n5o.1.1) so the epic view and ready_state share one batch accessor, and #172 delivered exactly that shared GetRelationsByIDs consumed by both, so the deferral was carried out rather than dropped.

The flag is a false positive: 71dd69a touched only the classifyChildStatus and openBlockerIDs comments, while the 'closed set of four variants' comment at line 15 is from the original commit. Go interfaces are not sealed, though the unexported marker() limits implementers to package cli, so the fix (reword to say exhaustiveness rests on locality) is accurate.
guidance_note: When a comment claims the type system enforces something, confirm the language actually enforces it (Go has no sealed interfaces) or say it is enforced by convention.

narrative: Round 0 raised two comment-accuracy findings about blocker ordering and an N+1. The agent fixed the comments and deferred the N+1 to a ticket, which #172 later delivered. The round-1 finding about the 'closed set' interface comment was in pre-review code and was not caused by the comment-fix commit. No fix caused a later finding.
guidance_observations: The N+1 deferral was legitimate because a ticket was filed and actually executed in the next epic PR; that pairing is what separates a defensible pushback from a dropped finding.

evidence: The fetch for closed children is wasted IO, but the PR already consolidated to one fetch per child, and the batch-accessor ticket n5o.1.1 (delivered in #172) is the real fix. A state-conditional skip would add a branch that the batch rewrite then removes.

sortStable called sort.Slice, so the name promised a property the code did not have. The agent renamed it to sortByEndpoints (657956a) and documented that (blocked, blocker) is a total order over distinct edges, which is right because the comparator alone guarantees determinism.
guidance_note: Name a function for what it guarantees (sortByEndpoints), not for a property of a different stdlib function (stable sort).

evidence: The flag is a false positive: 657956a only renamed the sort, while `internal := childIDSet(detail.Children)` is original PR code that omits the epic id, so a child-to-epic edge would surface as cross-epic. The fix (epicMemberIDs) is correct. The types-are-the-program citation is decoration because no type changed.
guidance_note: When defining a boundary set ('inside the epic'), enumerate every node that belongs to the boundary, including the root, and test an edge from each kind of member to the root.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: the hunk shows the original PR code using `Issue: child` and `classifyChildStatus(child, openBlockers(childDetail))`, which mixes the epic snapshot with the fresh detail. 657956a did not touch this. 0b0e0b7 switched both to childDetail.Issue.
guidance_note: After introducing a fresher per-row fetch, replace every read of the stale snapshot in that row, not just the reads the new feature needed.

evidence: This is a duplicate of F3, raised against 0b0e0b7 at 09:28 before d1828ff (epicMemberIDs) landed, so it is not caused by 0b0e0b7's change, which only switched to childDetail.Issue. The d1828ff diff confirms the epic id was added to the set.

The childIDSet comment 'the set of ids inside the epic' overstated what it contained; this is original code, not 0b0e0b7's change. d1828ff renamed it to epicMemberIDs with an accurate doc, as the diff shows.

This asked for a child-to-epic regression test. d1828ff adds TestRenderEpicContextEdgeToOwnEpicNotCrossEpic, which asserts no cross-epic section for that edge. The finding came from the stale-review race, not from 0b0e0b7.

d1828ff made the epic a member for exclusion (epicMemberIDs) but collect still visited only children, so the epic's own external edges were dropped; the agent conceded it was 'an inconsistency my previous commit introduced'. 667cf29 adds cross.collect(detail, internal) and a two-direction test.
guidance_note: When widening a membership set, find every operation that iterates the old members (here, collect over children) and extend it to the new member in the same commit.

evidence: After d1828ff changed the exclusion set to epic plus children, the openExcluding doc still said 'passing the epic's child ids'. 667cf29 updates it to 'the epic member ids (epic plus children)'.
guidance_note: When renaming or redefining a set, grep for prose that describes the old set (e.g. 'child ids') and update it in the same commit.

evidence: 667cf29 started calling collect on the epic detail, but collect's doc and parameter still said 'one internal child'. 794bd3a renamed the parameter to member and fixed the doc.
guidance_note: When a fix adds a new kind of caller to a function, reread that function's doc and parameter names for claims about who calls it.

narrative: Round 0 got a pushback on a closed-child IO optimization (deferred to the batch-accessor ticket) and a sort rename. Round 1 found two real original-code gaps: the epic missing from its own boundary set, and stale-snapshot reads. Round 2 re-raised the boundary gap against a commit that predated its fix. The epicMemberIDs fix then left collect visiting only children and left two docs describing the old set, which cost rounds 3 and 4.
guidance_observations: The F3 fix redefined 'inside the epic' but updated only one of the boundary's two consumers (exclusion, not collection) and none of the prose that described the old set; a grep for every use of the set and every comment naming it would have saved two rounds.
Round 2 was three duplicate findings caused by the review running against a commit pushed just before the fix; the already_fixed replies were correct and cheap.

evidence: `epic := epicRels[epicID]` ignores ok, and GetRelationsByIDs omits missing subjects, so an unknown id would render a zero-value epic where GetIssueDetail used to return NotFound. ab91368 adds the ok check returning store.NotFoundError.
guidance_note: When replacing a fail-loud single fetch with a lenient batch map, check ok on every subject the old path required to exist.

evidence: `childRel := childRels[child.ID]` ignores ok, which would append a zero-value Issue row. ab91368 fails with NotFoundError; the agent chose fail-loud over the reviewer's alternative 'or explicitly skip', which matches the prior GetIssueDetail contract.
guidance_note: When replacing a fail-loud single fetch with a lenient batch map, check ok on every subject the old path required to exist.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: ab91368 touched only epic_context.go, and listRelationsForIDs with its unfiltered `WHERE src_id IN (...) OR dst_id IN (...)` query is original PR code. Selecting related-to rows contradicts the 'structural' doc and hydrates extra endpoints. The fix filters to blocks and parent-child in SQL.
guidance_note: When documenting an accessor as returning a subset (structural edges), make the query enforce that subset rather than filtering downstream or not at all.

evidence: The F1/F2 fix (ab91368) added presence checks only in epic_context.go, while ready_state's fetchIssueRelations, the other consumer of the same lenient GetRelationsByIDs migrated in this PR, still returned the raw map indexed without ok. The agent itself called the fix 'symmetric with the epic-view presence checks'.
guidance_note: When fixing a missing-key hole at one consumer of a shared lenient accessor, sweep every consumer of that accessor in the diff (here, ready_state.go) in the same commit.

narrative: Round 0 caught the batch accessor's omit-missing contract silently producing zero-value rows in the epic view. The fix covered only the epic view, so round 1 found the same hole in the ready pipeline, alongside an unrelated original-code finding about unfiltered relation types. Round 1 would have happened anyway because of F3, so no round was avoidable.
guidance_observations: Changing an accessor's failure contract (fail-loud to omit) requires auditing every caller migrated in the same PR; the agent audited the one it was pointed at.

evidence: The prerequisites list Go and dolt but not just, yet the command block led with `just build` / `just install`. 93c4c65 leads with go build and ./scripts/install.sh.
guidance_note: Before publishing setup docs, check every command in the block against the listed prerequisites.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: the `golangci-lint run` line is from the original commit, and 93c4c65 only reordered the build and install lines. golangci-lint was indeed absent from the prerequisites, though calling it a setup blocker overstates a lint step.
guidance_note: Before publishing setup docs, check every command in the block against the listed prerequisites.

evidence: 93c4c65 added 'just build and just install are shortcuts for the first two commands', but per the reviewer the Justfile runs `go build -buildvcs=false`, so the new prose misdescribed the code it pointed at. 97250bb dropped the equivalence claim.
guidance_note: When a fix adds a claim about what another file does ('X is a shortcut for Y'), open that file and confirm the claim before pushing.

evidence: 97250bb introduced `[justfile](justfile)` while the tracked file is `Justfile`; the agent confirmed macOS case-insensitivity hid the 404 locally.
guidance_note: When a doc fix adds a repo-relative link, copy the path from `git ls-files` output so case matches on case-sensitive hosts.

narrative: A CONTRIBUTING.md PR in which each doc fix introduced a new inaccuracy. Making just optional added a wrong 'shortcut for' equivalence claim, and fixing that added a lowercase justfile link that 404s on GitHub. Round 1 also carried an independent golangci-lint nit, so only round 2 is strictly avoidable.
guidance_observations: Every new factual sentence in a doc fix was written without opening the file it described; checking each fix's new claims against the repo would have ended the PR a round earlier.

evidence: The hunk shows `+` (an empty line) before `# Contributor Covenant Code of Conduct`. 2d84686 stripped the leading and trailing blank lines and left the conduct text unchanged.
guidance_note: When vendoring text verbatim from an external source, normalize leading and trailing whitespace to repo convention before committing.

narrative: A single whitespace nit on a vendored Code of Conduct. The fix also handled the suppressed trailing-blank-line note, and round 1 was clean.

evidence: `if ! grep -qE ... CHANGELOG.md` treats grep's exit 2 (file missing) the same as no match, so a missing file would report 'has no ## [X.Y.Z] section'. 9176acd adds a separate `[[ -r CHANGELOG.md ]]` check.
guidance_note: When gating on grep's exit status, distinguish exit 1 (no match) from exit 2 (error) or pre-check the file, so each failure prints its own cause.

evidence: 9176acd tests `[[ ! -r CHANGELOG.md ]]` (missing or unreadable) but prints 'CHANGELOG.md not found at repo root', so the new message mismatches the condition it reports.
guidance_note: When writing an error message for a new guard, word it from the predicate actually tested (-r means readable, not exists).

evidence: The flag is a false positive: 9176acd touched only scripts/release.sh, and the 'build-time `ldflag` version stamping' line is from the original CHANGELOG.md commit. The Go flag is -ldflags.
guidance_note: When naming a CLI flag in prose, copy it from the command that uses it rather than retyping it.

narrative: The release-gate fix for a misleading grep failure introduced a message that said 'not found' for a readability check. Round 1 also caught an independent ldflag typo, so the round was not avoidable. Both were small and correctly fixed.

evidence: The topic membership was stated in quickstartTopics, QuickstartGuidanceNames, and the quickstartUsage const, so adding a topic required three edits. The fix deleted QuickstartGuidanceNames and derived both the refresh list and the usage string from the table; round-1 review confirms all derive from quickstartTopics.
guidance_note: When introducing a data table that enumerates a set, grep for every other enumeration of that set (helper lists, usage strings) and derive them from the table in the same commit.

narrative: One real one-source-of-truth finding: topic membership was declared in three places. The fix collapsed them into the table. Rounds 1 and 2 approved with non-blocking body notes and raised no inline findings.

evidence: maybeSyncAfterMutation checks only outcome.pushErr, and the function's own doc promises failures are 'surfaced loudly out-of-band'. A traceErr was dropped; the fix prints it to stderr.
guidance_note: When consuming a multi-error outcome struct, handle every error field it carries, not just the one the current branch is about.

narrative: The reviewer caught outcome.traceErr being dropped on the new on-change path; the fix was correct and round 1 approved. The same traceErr-drop gap reappeared in the next PR (#227, F2/F6) in the detached mirror, so the lesson did not carry over.
guidance_observations: A gap fixed here (dropping syncPushOutcome.traceErr) recurred in #227's new consumer of the same struct one PR later; a fix to one consumer of a multi-error result should prompt a note or helper that every consumer uses.

evidence: The original comment claimed `!synced` was 'the same skip lit sync push already makes', but performSyncPush skips only an empty remote (RemoteHasRefs), so the mirror diverged from the manual push. 5a74cf3 narrowed it to `synced && ahead == 0`. The cited law is about branching versus values, not about which predicate is right.
guidance_note: When a comment says a new path makes 'the same skip' as an existing one, reuse that existing gate instead of re-deriving a proxy for it.

evidence: recordMirrorError did `_, _ = maybeRecordAutomatedCommandTrace(...)`, discarding the trace-write error. The fix printed it to stderr, but stderr was nil in the detached spawn (`cmd.Stdin, cmd.Stdout, cmd.Stderr = nil, nil, nil`), so the fix was itself unobservable (see F5).
guidance_note: Before routing an error to a channel as the fix, confirm that channel is attached in the process that will run it; a detached worker with nil stderr has no stderr.

evidence: The agent kept the os.FindProcess placeholder and only rewrote its comment, arguing a real probe was code 'CI can neither compile nor run'. In F12 it then wrote the OpenProcess/GetExitCodeProcess probe and 'compile-checked for GOOS=windows in isolation', which refutes the unverifiability claim. The timeout-abort fix from F4 was sound but did not answer this finding.
guidance_note: Before declining a platform fix as unverifiable, try the cheap check (GOOS=windows go vet on the one file); if it compiles, ship the correct probe.

evidence: waitForProcessExit returned nothing on timeout and runBackgroundMirror proceeded to OpenSync regardless. 5a74cf3 makes it return a bool and records an error trace on false, and adds TestWaitForProcessExitReportsTimeout.
guidance_note: When a wait has a timeout, make it return whether the awaited condition held, and gate the dependent step on that result.

evidence: 5a74cf3's recordMirrorError fallback writes to stderr, while spawnBackgroundMirror still set Stderr to nil; the agent conceded 'my round-1 stderr fallback is unobservable while the worker's stderr is nil'. 596506d routes the worker's streams to <storage>/mirror.log.
guidance_note: Before routing an error to a channel as the fix, confirm that channel is attached in the process that will run it; a detached worker with nil stderr has no stderr.

evidence: mirrorOnce checked outcome.pushErr and dropped outcome.traceErr. That is the same swallowed-trace-error class F2 fixed in recordMirrorError and the exact gap #226/F1 fixed in maybeSyncAfterMutation one PR earlier. The F2 fix did not sweep it, and 596506d prints traceErr.
guidance_note: When fixing a swallowed trace error in one function, grep every consumer of maybeRecordAutomatedCommandTrace and of syncPushOutcome.traceErr in the same commit.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: 596506d touched only sync_bg.go, and the `compact bool` on SyncPush is original PR code. The mode bit is a real smell, but the original ran compact and push 'under one commit-lock acquisition'. Following the reviewer's 'split compaction into a separate caller' (acef9bf) gave up that atomicity and pushed the bit up a level, which started the F9→F11→F13 cascade; it ended at SyncCompactAndPush, an atomic variant passed as a value, which was available at this step.
guidance_note: When a reviewer proposes splitting an operation, first list the invariants the fused version held (here, one lock across GC and push) and pick a shape that keeps them.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: 596506d did not touch the freshness gate, which is original code narrowed by F1's 5a74cf3. A pre-check is a defensible optimization, but mirrorAhead duplicated performSyncPush's remote and branch resolution, so deleting it (acef9bf) removed real duplication along with the branch.
guidance_note: Before adding a pre-check ahead of a shared operation, check whether that operation already owns the skip decision, and reuse it rather than re-resolving its inputs.

evidence: acef9bf removed `compact` from SyncPush but added `if compact { syncStore.SyncCompact(ctx) }` inside performSyncPush, moving the same mode bit up one level. 76341e4 removed the parameter.
guidance_note: When removing a mode bit because the reviewer objects to the branch, trace the bit to the caller and remove it there too; relocating the branch is not removing it.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: `cmd.Env = append(os.Environ(), ...)` is original spawnBackgroundMirror code, and 76341e4 touched only performSyncPush call sites. The leaked LNKS_AUTOMATION_TRACE_REF_FILE would clobber the parent's handoff file, which 5dc7dfb's mirrorEnv strips. That is an inherited-ambient-state bug rather than duplicated truth, so the citation is a stretch.
guidance_note: When spawning a child process with os.Environ(), list which inherited variables name parent-owned output files and strip them.

evidence: 76341e4 (the F9 fix) moved SyncCompact to runSyncPush ahead of performSyncPush. The acef9bf comment it deleted stated the invariant, that compaction runs 'past the skip checks above, so it never garbage-collects for a push that won't happen', so a no-remote push started running DOLT_GC. The flagged commit 5dc7dfb is just the head at review time.
guidance_note: When moving a call, carry the invariants stated in the comment you are deleting to the new site, and check each one there.

evidence: This is the F3 Windows-liveness defect re-raised because F3 was answered with a comment rewrite only. b5e1e9b implements OpenProcess(PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION) plus GetExitCodeProcess (alive iff 259), the probe F3 asked for.
guidance_note: Before declining a platform fix as unverifiable, try the cheap check (GOOS=windows go vet on the one file); if it compiles, ship the correct probe.

evidence: b5e1e9b ran SyncCompact after performSyncPush returned, in a separate lock acquisition. The single-lock compact plus push had already been lost in acef9bf (F7's fix), and this placement made the interleave window explicit. 0689bb2's SyncCompactAndPush restores one runSyncMutation.
guidance_note: When moving a call, carry the invariants stated in the comment you are deleting to the new site, and check each one there.

narrative: Nine rounds on the detached on-change mirror. Round 0's real findings were mostly fixed correctly, but the trace-error fix wrote to a nil stderr and missed the sibling traceErr drop, which #226 had already fixed elsewhere. The Windows-probe pushback came back in round 5 and was then fixed in the way first declined. The compact mode-bit finding started a four-step cascade: split out (losing the single-lock atomicity), bit moved up, compaction before skip checks, compaction after lock release, finally SyncCompactAndPush, which keeps the original atomicity with the variant as a value. Rounds 1, 3, 5 and 6 consisted entirely of fix-caused findings.
guidance_observations: The compaction cascade came from adopting the reviewer's proposed cure verbatim at F7 without listing what the fused code guaranteed (one lock, no GC on skip); both invariants were written in comments the fixes deleted.
Each fix was checked against the finding it answered, not against the comments it removed; acef9bf's own 'past the skip checks' sentence named the invariant 76341e4 then broke.
A pushback built on 'unverifiable' (F3) was reversed two rounds later with a compile check the agent could have run the first time.

evidence: The reviewer assumed Synced reflects git ref existence. The agent showed it queries dolt_remote_branches, which DOLT_FETCH populates only from Dolt data, and reproduced against a bare remote with two git branches and no Dolt data: init did not adopt and doctor reported 'never synced'. The packet's repro output supports the pushback.

narrative: One finding conflated git refs with the Dolt remote-tracking ref. The agent refuted it with an empirical repro and named the regression test, then merged.
guidance_observations: The pushback is a model of the form: it named the exact query Synced runs, reproduced the reviewer's scenario, and pasted the output.

evidence: The function doc already carries the failure-mode rationale, and the inline 'Stage a write into the working set: begin a tx, write, commit the tx...' narrates code mechanics. ef1bbd4 replaced it with the one why-line about the tx not being DOLT_COMMIT'd.
guidance_note: When a test function's doc already states the rationale, keep inline comments to the one non-obvious fact per step (why the tx is not DOLT_COMMIT'd), not a walkthrough.

narrative: A test-only PR with one narration-comment finding, trimmed correctly. Round 1 approved.
